identity.name: Disodium 5'-ribonucleotides
synonyms: Mixture of disodium inosine-5'-monophosphate and disodium guanosine-5'-monophosphate
identity.chemical_class: Mixture of purine nucleotide salts (IMP/GMP sodium salts)

function.mechanism: The IMP/GMP components synergistically enhance umami (glutamate) perception and can increase perceived saltiness in formulated foods.

adi.basis: EFSA-accessible text cites SCF (1990) group ADI as 'not specified' for ribonucleotides (E626-E635); dedicated EFSA re-evaluation page was unavailable in this run.

efsa.key_finding: E635 is listed among authorized ribonucleotides in EU context; historical SCF ADI-not-specified basis is cited, and re-evaluation context is described as ongoing in EFSA text.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (WHO/JECFA entry for DISODIUM 5'-RIBONUCLEOTIDES; Food Additives Series 6).

concerns.summary: JECFA monograph notes that high intakes can increase serum and urinary uric acid, with specific caution for gout-prone individuals and those taking uric-acid-retaining diuretics.
Recent PubMed literature is mostly sensory/food formulation work (umami/saltiness modulation), with limited modern chronic toxicity studies specific to E635 as consumed in foods.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA historical long-term rat and dog studies reported no significant treatment-related abnormalities at tested dietary concentrations.
JECFA reproduction and teratogenicity studies in rats/mice/monkeys reported no significant fetal effects at tested doses.
JECFA retained ADI as 'not specified' for disodium 5'-ribonucleotides.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI was set (ADI 'not specified'), so classical ADI exceedance quantification is not available; concern is subgroup sensitivity to purine load at high intake.

risk_assessment.rationale: Core regulatory signals remain permissive (JECFA ADI not specified; U.S. CFR approvals of component salts), and no IARC listing was found. Main caveat is uric-acid sensitivity at high purine intake and sparse modern additive-specific chronic toxicity literature.
key_factors: JECFA ADI not specified with historical toxicology package
U.S. CFR permits disodium guanylate and disodium inosinate under intended-use conditions
JECFA notes uric-acid increase concern for susceptible subgroups
Dedicated EFSA E635 re-evaluation page was inaccessible in this run
